text_layer_notes: Quotes are as in the PDF text layer, which drops the fi/fl ligatures (e.g. "arti cial", "signi cantly") and joins hyphenated line breaks with a space.

table1.caption: Light treatment details. Light intensities were measured at the vertical level of the dummy female.

table2.caption: Estimates, z-values and p-values of pairwise treatment comparisons of numbers of attracted males using a negative binomial GLMM, with replicate night and site included as random factors.

table3.caption: Male attraction success of dummy females in the different light treatments. Treatments with a different letter (A or B) were significantly different from each other (logistic regression). N = 60 in all treatments except in the yellow-light treatment N = 59.

table4.caption: Estimates, z-values and p-values of a binomial GLMM assessing whether the dummy female attracted at least one male, with replicate night and site included as random factors.

abstract_treatments.quote: Each dummy was illuminated from above by either a blue (peak wavelength: 452 nm), white (449 nm), yellow (575 nm), or red (625 nm) LED lighting, or light switched off in the control.
abstract_treatments.label: documented

abstract_result.quote: with short wavelengths (blue and white) decreasing it more than long wavelengths (yellow and red).
abstract_result.label: documented

site_and_dates.quote: All work was conducted in Southern Finland in the proximity of Tvärminne Zoological Station (N 59°51′, E 23°14′), during the glow-worm breeding season, between 12th June and 4th July in 2020.
site_and_dates.label: documented

nights.quote: The experiment was run only on nights of good weather (N = 20 nights)
nights.label: documented

dummy_led.quote: Its peak wavelength was 562 nm, which matches the glow of female glow-worms (550–570 nm)
dummy_led.label: documented

dummy_intensity.quote: to adjust the intensity to 0.065–0.075 μWnm−1 (microwatts per nanometer)
dummy_intensity.label: documented

light_heights.quote: the light sources were attached at the following heights above the ground: 100 cm (blue), 110 cm (yellow), 120 cm (white), and 120 cm (red)
light_heights.label: documented

design.quote: We ran 3 repli- cates of each of the 5 treatments per night. Over the course of the exper- iment, we completed 4 replicates of each treatment at each of the 15 sites. This resulted in 60 replicates per treatment (over 20 nights), except for the yellow treatment, in which one replicate was discarded due to battery failure.
design.label: documented

timing.quote: We activated the arti cial lights and dummy females each night be- tween 23:45 and 00:15 and turned them off between 01:45 and 02:15.
timing.label: documented

recaptures.quote: recaptured males were not in- cluded in the data analyses
recaptures.label: documented

total_males.quote: The dummy females attracted a total of 624 male glow-worms during the experiment.
total_males.label: documented

medians.quote: The median number of males attracted was two in the control, yel- low and red light treatments, and zero in the blue and white light treat- ments (Fig. 2).
medians.label: documented

success_total.quote: Over the whole experiment, 56.9 % (170/299) of the dummy females attracted at least one male.
success_total.label: documented

count_result.quote: Dummy females in the blue and white light treatments attracted signi cantly fewer males than dummy females in the yellow, red and control treatments (Fig. 2, Table 2).
count_result.label: documented

fig2_n.quote: N = 60 in all treatments except N = 59 in the yellow light treatment.
fig2_n.label: documented

not_reported: Table S1, Fig. S1 (treatment spectra), Fig. S2: supplementary files, not in this PDF and not obtained. The paper gives peak wavelengths only, no spectra.
Fig. 2 (box plots of males per trap): drawn only; the trap table holds the underlying counts.

Which source row is the discarded yellow replicate: the paper says one yellow replicate was discarded (battery failure); the trap table has one row with every field "NA" (night 10, site 3). The file does not say they are the same row.
Model estimates are on the model scale (link function not restated in the tables); kept as printed.
